steps.text: Blend red wine vinegar, honey, mustard, lime juice, pepper, salt, paprika, garlic, onion, oregano, and sugar together in a blender until thoroughly mixed. Drizzle olive oil into mixture while blending on low. Chill at least 1 hour before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Smoked Paprika Vinaigrette
raw_recipe.description: This tangy smoked paprika vinaigrette with mustard, honey, lime, and garlic makes a great salad dressing and a great marinade!
raw_recipe.name: Smoked Paprika Vinaigrette

recipeInstructions.text: Blend red wine vinegar, honey, mustard, lime juice, pepper, salt, paprika, garlic, onion, oregano, and sugar together in a blender until thoroughly mixed. Drizzle olive oil into mixture while blending on low. Chill at least 1 hour before serving.

review.reviewBody: Fabulous dressing - another winner from AR! I didn't have smoked paprika so I used regular (this will give me an excuse to go buy some). Other than the regular paprika I followed the recipe exactly and put everthing into a mini food processor and let it go. Just the right amount of sweet and tang - I can't wait to try the smokey version! UPDATE: I went out and bought smoked paprika and OMG this stuff is amazing! I'm hooked!
My husband and I love this recipe. I do use avocado oil instead of the olive oil and omit the sugar and lime juice. We like it with a kick so we add Sriracha to it. We use this all the time. Try it!

This was so yummy and different! I mixed everything in my mini-processor, subbed a shallot for the onion and I reduced the honey at first to just 2 tbsp, thinking this would be too sweet. However, I think it needed the full amount - I added more before serving and it was delicious! I had bought hot smoked paprika but hardly ever use it - thanks for giving me another reason!

This is wonderful. I left out the onion and sugar and added 2 tbs of Franks Red Hot to tone down the sweetness. I marinated a chuck roast and braised it with a little white wine and onion slices. It will be a fantastic dressing on raw veggie salad and I can't wait to marinate some chicken breasts with it. Thank you for sharing.

Great dressing even my fiance liked it and he doesn't really care for vinaigrette style dressings! I didn't have smoked paprika so I used regular and I had some liquid smoke so I just added a 1/4tsp of that and it worked perfectly. Also I didnt have stone ground mustard and I substituted with spicy brown. I also used only 1/3 cup of olive oil instead of 1/2 cup and it was a little tangy, but I love tangy plus less fat!

This dressing is really good. It is really sweet though, even though I didn't add the tsp of white sugar. I also didn't blend it, just very finely minced the onion and garlic. Would recommend adding more garlic, for a more spicy flavor and a little less honey. But really delicious!

I wanted something different to put on pasta salad and made this up for it. I used regular paprika. Gives a nice sweet tart taste and something different for the pasta. Really good flavor and easy, I just whisked it up in the bowl. I didn't have stone ground mustard, that would have made it even better! Thanks DCGirlyGirl.

I wanted something different to put on pasta salad and made this up for it. I used regular paprika. Gives a nice sweet tart taste and something different for the pasta. Really good flavor and easy, I just whisked it up in the bowl. I didn't have stone ground mustard, that would have made it even better! Thanks DCGirlyGirl.

Off the charts delicious! I was in a big hurry to whip up some salad dressing after putting taco salad on the table for dinner and realized I was completely out. This recipe sounded wonderful so I gave it a shot. I cheated and used onion and garlic powders, used Dijon mustard because that's what I had, and used half chipotle powder to give it a little kick, and half smoked paprika. I also cut back on the vinegar a little and made up the difference with more lime juice. It didn't need any sugar, the honey was just perfect.

This recipe was very good. I did not have any coarse/brown mustard so I substituted yellow mustard and it worked well. With the milder mustard the dressing did not need any sugar as the honey provided enough balance.

Great dressing to go with Sue's Taco Salad from this site. I used a small whisk to combine the ingredients and as I added the olive oil with no problem. I just used garlic powder and onion powder just because I didn't feel like dealing with the real thing. Worked fine. Very good and unusual dressing.
I made exactly as written and served over a tossed spinach salad. Yum!
Absolutely loved it! My wife, the acknowledged queen of the dressings, thought it was fantastic. Highly recommend.

I really enjoy this dressing. 
There is just the right amount of sweetness to balance out the vinegar.
So yummy! Me new go to favorite!
It turned out good but believe the next time I would add a bit more sugar or honey.
Nice recipe, but I'd increase the amount of smoked paprika--you barely taste it! Also, it is quite tart, so maybe increase the sugar, like the cook's note recommended.
Very tasty. I made this dressing for my caprese salad!
This is excellent. We made it almost as is. I was out of olive oil so I used vegetable oil. We served it with grilled chicken, roasted corn and avocado and tortilla chips. Yum!
I added everything to the VitaMix and turned it on high for a minute or two. A very tasty blend of sweet and tart. I will definitely make this again and again.
